label: copy-phase input k (not the first original token)
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase, when the fed-back input token is the letter k, i.e. while re-reading a k that was original token 1 or later (recall_idx >= 2). It never fires in the original phase or on the delimiter, never on any other input token, and essentially never when k was the first original token (that is, input at recall_idx 1; 16 tiny activations). Magnitude is largest when k sat at original position 2-3 (recall_idx 3-4, which hold about 59% of mass, with top examples near the max). It is weaker when k was original token 1 (recall_idx 2): rate is lower there and most false positives (about 15% of predicted steps are inactive) are k at original index 1 in short sequences. Output token, prior tokens and repeat counts have little effect.

issues: Core claims hold. On the dev split all activation is in the copy phase (share 1.000) and in_tok==k (share 1.000). At recall_idx 1 there are 16 activations with 0 mass (21 on test, also 0% of mass). recall_idx 3-4 carry 0.333+0.254=0.587 of the mass. Test P=0.852, R=0.9997, F1=0.920, mass recall 0.99994, which matches the reported scores.

The explanation overstates where the false positives come from. Steps at recall_idx==2 account for about 4.5k of the 11.0k test false positives (about 41%), not 'most'. The rest are spread out. Precision rises steadily with L: L=3 is 0.09, L=4 is 0.65, L=9 is 0.91. It also dips at the last copy step (to_go==0 precision 0.76; r=6,L=7 is 0.60). So the feature is weaker on k in short sequences and on the final output step generally, not just at original index 1.

L=3 is close to a dead zone: only 38 of 423 predicted k steps are active, plus 38 activations at t=5 on dev. It is small in volume, and excluding it gives only a negligible gain (test F1 0.9224 vs 0.9200).

No clean subset of the false positives could be cut without losing recall. Excluding the last step for L<=7 gives F1 0.872. Excluding (r==2 & L<=4) together with L>=4 gives F1 0.920. Repeat counts (in_count) and copy correctness do not separate the false positives either. The remaining false positives look like a graded dependence on magnitude rather than a missing condition.
